artists.biography: Stiff Little Fingers are a punk rock band from Belfast, Northern Ireland. They formed in 1977, at the height of the Troubles. They started out as a schoolboy band called Highway Star (named after the Deep Purple song), doing rock covers, until they discovered punk. They split up after six years and four albums, although they reformed five years later, in 1987. Despite major personnel changes, they are still touring and recording as of 2011. Jake Burns, their lead singer, is the only member to have been with the band during all its incarnations, but in March 2006, original bass guitarist Ali McMordie rejoined them following the departure of The Jam bass player Bruce Foxton after fifteen years.

perplexity.description:
Released in 1979 on Rough Trade Records (not Parlophone), Inflammable Material is the debut album by Northern Irish punk band Stiff Little Fingers. The album is a defining work of the UK punk rock movement, characterized by its raw, energetic sound, urgent guitar riffs, and politically charged lyrics. Drawing from the band’s experiences growing up during The Troubles in Belfast, the songs confront themes of sectarian violence, social deprivation, and police brutality, offering a stark and authentic portrayal of life in Northern Ireland at the time. Musically, the album blends fast-paced punk with melodic hooks and a sense of immediacy, influenced by bands like The Clash but distinguished by its regional perspective and lyrical honesty.

Inflammable Material holds a pivotal place in Stiff Little Fingers’ discography as their first full-length statement and remains their most influential release. It was the first album released by an independent label to reach the UK Top 20, peaking at number 14, and helped pave the way for the rise of independent music in Britain. The album received widespread critical acclaim for its intensity, authenticity, and social commentary, cementing Stiff Little Fingers’ reputation as one of punk’s most important bands. Its legacy endures as a landmark record in both punk and Irish rock history.
